newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico peso weakens sharply again on speculation.
newsitem.headline: Mexico peso weakens sharply again on speculation.

text.p: The Mexican peso opened sharply weaker across the board on Thursday, hit once more by mounting speculation and nerves in a market with demand for dollars in short supply, traders said.
"It's the same old story. There's a run on the peso because of nerves and speculation. People want dollars, but there aren't any," a trader said.
The benchmark 48-hour peso and its 24-hour counterpart were 5.5 and 4.5 centavos weaker, respectively, at 8.0450/8.0660 and 8.0300/8.0450 per dollar.

Traders said that the market was concerned over the possible contents of the budget and the government's official economic policy criteria for 1997. Those issues will be laid out sometime in November.
Furthermore, traders said that many dealers were cautious in the run-up to U.S. presidential and congressional elections on November 5, and the Federal Open Market Committe meeting on November 13.
"Dealers are trying to justify speculation any way they can, but the fact is that many made a loss yesterday and are now trying to make up for it today," said a trader.
Traders said the 48-hour peso faced an important support level at 8.10 per dollar.
"What they seem to be doing is pushing it to 8.10 per dollar, in order to sell when it gets there," said another trader.
